Subject: Weekly pipeline -> fleet signal: May 12–19 handoff

Team — attaching the latest pipeline slice (CSV) and our capacity assumptions PDF. Goal: convert the forecast into a concrete GPU reserve ask for the infra plan next week. Key points:  

- Top three near-term opportunities (ACME pilot, Orion POC, Helix beta) show simultaneous token-constrained windows between Jun 8–25.
- Current sales forecast (best case) implies ~420 GPU-hours/day at p95 over a 2-week ramp unless we apply prefix caching and batching (see assumptions file).
- Finance is flagging that we should avoid >60% committed reserved spend unless there is a signed 12-month commitment.

Please review and reply with: 1) a recommended reserved slot ask (GPU count + expected start week), 2) any infra constraints we should call out to Sales when we engage procurement, and 3) the minimum SLA band we can promise if we shift some capacity to burst. I will consolidate and share with ACME procurement on Friday.

Attachments: 20260512-pipeline-forecast.csv (CSV), capacity-assumptions-may2026.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Mina

On Tue, 12 May 2026 at 09:02 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — attaching the latest pipeline slice (CSV) and our capacity assumptions PDF. Goal: convert the forecast into a concrete GPU reserve ask for the infra plan next week.
>
Short notes from ops perspective:  
- Using the forecast and the latency targets, my back-of-envelope says we need 12 reserved A100-equivalent slots for the ACME pilot window to hit p95 SLA without burst. If we accept a 20% tail latency increase we can drop to 8 reserved and rely on burst.
- Burst capacity is available but throttled by region; if ACME wants EU fallbacks we'll need cross-region routing play.
- Lead time for adding reserved slots (procurement + infra config) is ~3 weeks on our current queue.

Action: I recommend we ask Sales for a week-by-week reserved ramp rather than a single start date (example: 4 slots week1, 8 slots week2, 12 slots week3). That buys flexibility and lowers short-term commit.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly pipeline -> fleet signal: May 12–19 handoff

Thanks Ben — that ramp looks sensible from sales. A couple of context bullets from my side:  
- ACME's procurement timeline: they want a signed MSA by Jun 1 to hit a Jun 15 pilot start. We should assume 2–3 weeks to finalize SOW and procurement after MSA signature.
- Revenue profile: pilot -> production conversion expected in Q3; if pilot hits latency/cost targets they will move to a 12-month committed tier.
- Sales preference: incremental weeks are easier to justify to procurement (phased commitment).

Requested from Finance: Stephanie, can you confirm whether a phased commitment (ramp) is acceptable for revenue recognition and whether we can structure the deal so that later weeks convert to a fixed reserved commitment? If not, we should be explicit to ACME.

Karthik
From: Sabrina Holt <sabrina.holt@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 08:44:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Weekly pipeline -> fleet signal: May 12–19 handoff

Thanks Mina — quick clarifying Qs from ACME procurement/ops:  
1) If we sign the MSA by Jun 1 and start the pilot Jun 15, what SLA do you guarantee for p95 latency for the pilot? Is that the reserved-only SLA or burst-inclusive?
2) Can you provide a week-by-week capacity ramp that maps to invoice line items? Procurement prefers concrete dollar buckets for each week.

We can accept a phased ramp but need explicit dollar and SLA bands per phase. Happy to hop on a 30-min call next week to align.

—Sabrina Holt
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Holt <sabrina.holt@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly pipeline -> fleet signal: May 12–19 handoff (summary + next steps)

Team and Sabrina — thanks for the quick-turn responses. Consolidated summary and next steps:  

Summary decisions
- Ask: phased reserved ramp for ACME pilot (4 -> 8 -> 12 slots across the 3-week pilot ramp). Ben confirmed infra lead time ~3 weeks; propose start week Jun 15.
- SLA band for pilot: reserved-only p95 commitment for weeks where reserved slots are active; for weeks using burst we'll provide best-effort p95 with a defined fallback (cross-region routing) and a 20% latency allowance. We will include that language in the SOW.
- Finance constraints: Stephanie to confirm structure by EOD Wed 5/20 (convertibility of ramp into a 12-month commit).

Action items
- Stephanie Nguyen: confirm finance treatment and preferred invoicing cadence (weekly line items vs. aggregated milestone). Due: 2026-05-20 EOD.
- Ben Carter: create infra runbook for phased ramp including region failover notes and provisioning timeline. Due: 2026-05-26. Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AEXAMPLE/pipeline-playbook
- Laura Bennett / Karthik Iyer: align with ACME procurement on MSA/SOW language and share draft with Mina. Due: 2026-05-21. HubSpot: 1347291

I will send a short SOW template to Sabrina with the phased cost lanes once Stephanie confirms invoicing. If anyone needs to flag a hard blocker to the schedule, reply-all within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Mina
